validation_note: An initial amd64 full run and repeated media diagnostics exposed intermittent Rosetta mmap failures while launching media helpers under the unchanged 2 GiB RLIMIT_AS safety bound. A disposable stderr-enabled diagnostic build identified the emulator error. It was discarded; final validation uses the original helper and the same limit. The failed runs are retained in the evidence. The final emulated run uses the same four-server-CPU affinity as native ARM64; earlier unrestricted-CPU emulated runs are retained. This is not a substitute for a native amd64 CI run, and the Rosetta limitation is not claimed to be fixed by application changes.
changes: Move the already parsed form into the posting handler. Posting uses its own existing transaction directly, avoiding a second form parse and the empty outer write transaction.

Check for eligible jobs with a read before attempting the atomic claim. Empty, delayed and already leased queues do not take a writer lock. The claim rechecks eligibility inside its UPDATE to preserve race safety.
Use a partial index for nonfailed jobs in claim order, avoiding a temporary sort. Schema initialization adds it idempotently to existing databases.

Renew a ten-minute job lease only when five minutes or less remain. The decision reads persisted state, so transaction rollback cannot leave a stale cached renewal. Each delivery receipt still commits separately.
deferred_architecture: A dedicated asynchronous SQLite writer remains a possible architectural improvement. Integrating it cleanly requires an explicit request/transaction ownership and scheduling design; no ad hoc RPC, SQL-text classifier, lock file or native callback bridge was added.
Rendering and event-size validation remain before commit so an oversized or invalid broadcast cannot leave an acknowledged partial mutation. Moving them later would need a separate admission design.
SQLite checkpoint behavior is unchanged. A background checkpointer needs bounded WAL growth and supervised lifecycle handling; this change does not add an unbounded timer-based shortcut.
validation: Both ARM64 native and amd64 emulated passed 81 application/operations cases, the new lease fixture, independent Rails/signing/session/crypto/JSON/binary vectors, and 10,000 native ASan/UBSan fuzz executions each. Both packaged images passed browser workflows, process restart, HTTPS/WSS/HTTP2, Disk migration, backup and restore. Shared paused-job and active-lease crash recovery passed for Rust, C and Mojo. CI syntax passed locally; the new tests run through tools/check.sh on both CI architectures. No remote CI was triggered.

metadata.order: rotating Latin-square order: Rust/C/Mojo, C/Mojo/Rust, Mojo/Rust/C
metadata.durability: SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL; atomic message/outbox; persisted retries and receipts; at-least-once recovery
metadata.completion: Post rate includes HTTP plus final job drain, exact message IDs and subscription receipt sets required
metadata.notifications: Three selected subscriptions/message; canonical notification preparation and identical endpoint-policy rejection; no remote push network in timed workloads

normalization: verified database ID to legacy client-ID DOM convention; new pending-only attributes

upstream_differences.difference: C joins the three direct-room initials with +; Rust uses an English sentence.
C joins the three direct-room initials with +; Rust uses an English sentence.

method: Apple M4 / 24 GiB, native ARM64 Linux in Docker Desktop. Three rotating rounds, 2-second warmups, 8-second samples, 16 keep-alive gzip clients, 64 MiB response caches. Servers and jobs share CPUs 0–3; client uses CPUs 4–7. SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL, atomic message/outbox writes, per-recipient durable receipts, common 10-second write-lock budget. Posting includes queue drain. No builds or other task tests ran during timing.
limits: Rust and C retain their existing local durability patches and were not modified in this task. Timed posts prepare three push recipients with the same endpoint-policy rejection; remote push encryption/network delivery and active Cable subscribers are outside these five timed workloads and have separate correctness tests. External delivery remains at-least-once after a crash between remote acceptance and recording its receipt. These are implementation measurements under one configuration, not intrinsic language speed.
